script.heading: Intro

articles.title: Patient-reported disability has insufficient clinical accuracy for predicting physical function in survivors of critical illness: a secondary analysis of a cluster-randomised trial.
articles.summary: This secondary analysis of the stepped-wedge cluster-randomised Enhanced Recovery after Intensive Care trial included patients from 10 German ICU clusters who completed the WHO Disability Assessment Schedule (WHODAS) 2.0 plus either HGS, the 2MWT, or both, 6 months after ICU discharge. The median HGS, expressed as a percentage of the expected value (%exp), was 70.6%exp (Q1, Q3: 54.4, 85.6), and the median 2MWT distance was 73.7%exp (Q1, Q3: 61.5, 85.8). The 2MWT was not completed by 59% of patients. In multivariable regression models, the WHODAS 2.0 sum score predicted HGS in kg (β: -0.27 [95% CI: -0.33 to -0.22]; P<0.001) and 2MWT distance in m (β: -1.94 [95% CI: -2.37 to -1.51]; P<0.001), but the limits of agreement exceeded the MCIDs. Post-ICU care often misses patients unable to attend in-person clinic visits.
